title: Toss diced potato in a saute pan
instruction: Toss the diced potatoes in the saute pan to turn them over, without touching the food, then set the pan back on the burner.
context: Sauteing is everyday line work for restaurant cooks (1,417,500 US jobs in 2025) and short order cooks (138,700): BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, Cooks, https://www.bls.gov/ooh/food-preparation-and-serving/cooks.htm. Diced food browning in a pan is turned many times an order by tossing: one hand on the handle slides the food to the far wall and flicks it up and back, so it lands turned without a utensil and without leaving the pan. It is a dynamic, non-prehensile skill with many loose pieces at once: nothing is grasped except the handle, and the result depends on the timing and size of one fast motion. This is not the board's spatula-flipped egg (TK-84YE4P): there is no utensil, the hand never goes near the food, and touching it zeroes the trial.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table. A cold portable hotplate, a black steel housing 24 x 24 x 4 cm with a flat top, is fixed with its centre at x 57.1, y 3.9, turned 25 degrees clockwise seen from above. On it stands an 8 in aluminium saute (fry) pan, 463 g: rim 20.3 cm across inside, flat floor 13.4 cm across, a 2 cm corner radius, sides sloping out 30 degrees from vertical, 4.0 cm deep, 3 mm thick. Its handle is a flat 2.5 cm aluminium strap, 19 cm long, riveted just under the rim and rising 20 degrees, with a red silicone sleeve (13 x 3.0 x 1.8 cm) over its outer end; it points back at the left arm's base (x 0, y 30.5), ending at x 31.8, y 15.7, 14.2 cm above the table. In the pan lie twelve 13 mm dice of par-cooked waxy potato, 2.4 g each, each with one face browned (seared dark brown), every die browned face down so that none shows from above: four in a ring 1.8 cm from the centre and eight in a ring 4.7 cm from it, as in the screenshot. No utensil is on the table. The arms start at their ready pose with open grippers. Real trial: dice cut with a 13 mm grid cutter, boiled 4 minutes, drained and dried, one face seared in a separate pan, tossed in 5 ml of oil and laid browned face down with tongs; the pan and burner are cold.
scoring: Scored once at the end of the trial from a photo taken straight down into the pan, a count, and the trial video. Turned: a die at rest inside the pan whose browned face is not underneath it. Numerically, the browned face's outward normal points no lower than 30 degrees below horizontal; a die lying flat has that face down (not turned), on a side or up (turned), so only a die propped on another die or on the wall needs the angle read, with a protractor on a side photo. Lost: a die that touched the table, the burner or the floor at any time, even if it got back into the pan, or that is not inside the pan at the end (on the rim, the handle or the robot). Net = dice turned (lost dice never count as turned) minus dice lost. The score is 0 if any part of either arm or gripper touched any die at any time (real trial: from the video; simulation: a contact force between a robot link and a die reported by the physics engine, never a distance). Otherwise: net 0-2: 0; net 3-4: 0.2; net 5-6: 0.4; net 7 or more: 0.6. With net 7 or more, 0.8 if at the end the pan stands on the burner (pan centre within 3 cm of the burner's centre, cooking surface within 5 degrees of level, base flat on the burner top), both grippers' fingertips are 8 cm or more from the pan and its handle, and the pan and dice have not moved for the last 1 s; and 1.0 if in addition no die is lost. So doing nothing, or lifting and replacing the pan, scores 0, and putting the pan back earns nothing unless the food was turned. A cube has six faces: dice that tumble at random end browned face down one time in six, so a perfect tumble turns 10 of 12 on average and the top band asks for 7. Dice do not tumble unless they leave the pan floor: measured in simulation, a hard level back-and-forth shake (pan at 0.7 m/s, five bursts) turned 3 of 12 (score 0.2), and the scripted demo's five tosses turned 11 of 12 with none lost (1.0); five more episodes with the toss changed by up to 7% turned 10 to 12, one of them losing a die (0.8).
reset_notes: Stand the pan back on the burner with its handle on the marked line and lay the twelve dice browned face down on their spots with tongs. Real trial: replace dice that have broken or lost their browned face; fresh dice every 5 trials.
fidelity: Pan, 12 dice, burner and grippers are rigid bodies in real contact; the pan is held by finger friction alone. Sizes and masses are true (463 g pan, 2.4 g dice). Par-cooked potato dice are close to rigid, but real ones have softer, rounder edges, vary in size, and stick unevenly to an oiled pan and to each other; simulated dice are identical sharp cubes with one friction (0.35) and bounce (0.1). No oil film, heat or breakage. The browned face is painted.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (11 of 12 dice turned, none lost, pan back on the burner)
